stem: Pallavi has two sticks of lengths $7\,\mathrm{cm}$ and $10\,\mathrm{cm}$. She wants a third stick of length $x\,\mathrm{cm}$ so the three lengths can form a triangle.

parts.text: Which claim about the third length $x$ is correct?

options.text: The answer is the phrase fixed side lengths.
$x$ must satisfy $3 < x < 17$, because $|10-7| < x < 10+7$ with the endpoints excluded.
$x$ may equal $3$ or $17$ as well as any value between them.
She must first construct the triangle with compass arcs, and only then decide which $x$ values are allowed.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: The triangle inequality requires $|10-7|<x<10+7$, so $3<x<17$; the endpoints are excluded because equality would leave a flat line, not a triangle.

teacher.key_rationale: Strict inequality 3<x<17 follows from |10−7|<x<10+7. Naming fixed sides, including the endpoints, or requiring a compass construction first all leave that range.
